content:
Apple has recently raised prices on most of its products, with more increases expected next month affecting iPhones and other devices.

The iPhone 18 lineup is expected to see price hikes, while Apple Watch and AirPods may also be affected.

Earlier this year, Apple raised prices on several of its products.

Mac, iPad, Apple TV, HomePod, and Vision Pro all saw price increases at the same time.

CEO Tim Cook previously warned that a wave of price increases was coming, but the breadth of the increases still comes as a surprise.

In the first round of price hikes, the following flagship products were the only ones not affected:

  • iPhone
  • Apple Watch
  • AirPods

At the time, Apple hinted that more price increases were on the way, and analysts also believed that the few products initially unaffected would not escape price hikes in the short term.

With the September iPhone 18 launch event approaching, the market widely expects iPhone prices to rise.

There are reports that the starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro will range from US$1,299 to US$1,399, compared with the current US$1,099 starting price of the iPhone 17 Pro.

Apple has historically lowered prices on older models when new devices are launched, but this year older models are expected to keep their prices unchanged or see slight increases.

The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 may also see price hikes, as the current AI-driven memory shortage crisis will also affect the cost of watch components.

As for AirPods, price hikes are also possible, but the likelihood is lower than for iPhone and Apple Watch, because AirPods are less affected by rising memory and storage chip costs.

However, if Apple plans to raise prices across its entire product line, including AirPods, the answer will be revealed at the September launch event.

What price changes do you expect from Apple? Let us know in the comments section.
